solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Missing the extremely strategic manoeuvres of the corporation?

definitions.note: corporation is jocular slang for a large belly, so this means relating to the stomach

indicators.note: manoeuvres says the remaining letters are moved about into a new order
missing says the picked letters are absent from the word they come out of
extremely points to the outermost letters of the word the, its first and last

explanation.surface: A company has bungled its strategy by skipping the extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing the extremely' strips T and E (the ends of 'the') from STRATEGIC, leaving SRAGIC... letters S,R,A,T,G,I,C, which 'manoeuvres' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is an old humorous word for a paunch, so belly-related is stomach-related: an adjective for the stomach.

clue.text: Need my stereo to be set up regularly

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, as is gosh!

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of stereo

explanation.surface: Someone needs their hi-fi installed at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, R, O from stereo; 'set up' turns them to ORT under GOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To go short is to lack or be in want of something, which is to need it.

clue.text: Van doing broadcast in position for good reception

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for a post or place

parts.note: a station is a position or post someone occupies

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words are scattered

explanation.surface: A van is being used for an outside broadcast from a spot with a strong signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns VAN DOING into NDINGOVA, which goes 'in' STA...TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer given a standing ovation has been received warmly: an enthusiastic audience welcome.

clue.text: Spaniard's crop introducing a cold feeling right away

definitions.note: read as Spaniard is, the name of a Spaniard

parts.note: a riding crop is a short whip or rod

indicators.note: right away says R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

parts.note: rigor is a sudden shivering fit, a feeling of cold with fever

explanation.surface: A Spanish farmer's harvest is hit by a sudden chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' drops the final R from RIGOR, leaving RIGO after ROD. Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodrigo is a Spanish given name and surname, borne for example by the composer Joaquín Rodrigo.

clue.text: Festival on Hawaii, perhaps, or somewhere further south

parts.note: Christmas is the Christian festival of 25 December
Hawaii is an example of an island, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Celebrating a holiday in the Pacific, or even further below the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two islands of this name: one in Kiribati, south of Hawaii, and an Australian one in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific atoll in Kiribati lies well south of Hawaii, a real place matching the vague location.

clue.text: Water in the east region's almost too centrally located

indicators.note: centrally located puts the shortened word into the middle of the other

parts.note: an area is a region; the 's reads as has

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: also means too, as well

explanation.surface: A body of water lies in an eastern region, placed too near the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ALSO to ALS, and 'centrally located' sets it in the middle of AREA: AR-ALS-EA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea is a shrinking inland body of water in Central Asia, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer lunches with a macabre crook

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or unwell, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady solicitor eats with a sinister criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a noun for a criminal, matching 'Dodgy lawyer', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer who chases accident victims for compensation cases is a byword for unscrupulous legal practice.

clue.text: What Sewell makes of Welles, and vice versa

definitions.text: What Sewell makes of Welles, and vice versa

parts.words: What Sewell makes of Welles, and vice versa
parts.note: the two names use the same six letters rearranged, so each is a rearrangement of the other

explanation.surface: One person's critical opinion of a famous film director, and his of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a critic such as Brian Sewell judging Orson Welles; in fact the names share their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewell and Welles contain identical letters in a different order, which is exactly what a word puzzle of rearrangement is.

clue.text: Landslides shan't hit remote parts of the UK

indicators.note: hit means struck or damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Landslips will not strike the far-flung corners of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern archipelago lies far beyond the Scottish mainland, among the most distant parts of the country.

clue.text: In the existing circumstances, American and European are stopping other nationals

indicators.note: stopping means plugging gaps, so the abbreviation is put inside the phrase
are, with stopping, says the pieces plug the phrase; here it governs the first of two insertions

parts.note: as is means in the present state, as things stand
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: Under the present conditions, people from America and Europe are blocking foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are stopping' puts US into the first part, A-US-S, and E into the second, I-E-S, of AS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aussies are Australians, nationals of a different country from those the surface names.

clue.text: Regular supporters make outstanding leaders

parts.note: standard means regular or normal
bearers are people who carry or support something

explanation.surface: Faithful fans make for excellent captains.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who carry the flag at the front are figuratively prominent leaders of a movement or cause.

clue.text: Invests in cloth

parts.note: the cloth is the clergy, so investing someone in it is making them a priest

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests buying textiles; 'the cloth' is the clergy, and invests means installs in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop admits people to holy orders, investing them with priestly office in the clergy.

clue.text: Temptress about to enter a text message that is rejected

indicators.note: to enter puts the short word for about inside the text abbreviation

parts.note: lol, laughing out loud, is a common text abbreviation
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A seductress is about to send a text that gets turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts RE in LOL; 'rejected' turns IE to EI. The Lorelei is the Rhine siren who lures boatmen to their doom.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend the Lorelei is a siren on the Rhine whose song lures sailors onto the rocks.

clue.text: Orders from on high influence soldiers under canvas?

indicators.note: under canvas means within a tent, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: tents are made of canvas, so canvas stands for tents
command is control or influence over others
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Commanders issue orders to troops who are camping.
explanation.walkthrough: COMMAND and MEN go inside TENTS: TEN-COMMANDMEN-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: These biblical laws were handed down by God to Moses on Sinai, literally commands from heaven.

clue.text: Foster patients here in the shower?

definitions.text: Foster patients here in the shower?

parts.words: Foster patients here in the shower?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme has Doctor Foster going to Gloucester in a shower of rain, so a doctor's patients would be in that county

explanation.surface: Asks whether a carer bathes their charges.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Doctor Foster went to Gloucester in a shower of rain'; Gloucestershire is an English county in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county contains the city of Gloucester, where the rhyme's doctor went in the rain.

clue.text: Reportedly criticise drug that is eaten

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the sound of the words matters

parts.note: knock means criticise, and E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Word is that someone is attacking a substance that has been swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOCK E said out loud sounds like the Italian dumplings, NYOK-ee.
explanation.definitionFit: These small Italian potato dumplings are a food, something one eats.

clue.text: No time for bed — take short nap in the best snug?

indicators.note: no time says T, the abbreviation for time, is removed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: Too busy for bed, someone grabs a quick doze in the warmest corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time for' drops T from COT, leaving CO; 'short' cuts SIESTA to SIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of snug or cosy means the warmest and most comfortable of all.

clue.text: Heath upset after tabloid's maximum exposure in this?

indicators.note: after puts the turned moor behind the newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

explanation.surface: A newspaper reveals a former prime minister's exposure in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MOOR into ROOM, placed 'after' SUN. The surface hints at Ted Heath, a UK prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory-like room with large windows is designed to let in as much sunlight as possible.

clue.text: Overwhelms crime prevention officers last seen touring Arab states

indicators.note: touring means going round, so these letters surround the other piece
last seen picks the final letter of each of the three words

parts.note: the Gulf is the collective name for the Arab states on the Persian Gulf

explanation.surface: Police crime-prevention officers were last spotted travelling round the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last seen' gives E, N, S, which go round GULF: EN-GULF-S.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swamp or submerge completely, as a flood overwhelms land.

clue.text: First lady once requiring rock band to grab poles

indicators.note: to, part of to grab, makes the band's name take in the second pole as well
grab means seize and hold, so the band's name takes in the first pole

parts.note: Oasis is a British rock band
N and S are the north and south poles
the second pole, S for south

explanation.surface: A former president's wife needs a band to support the Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' puts N after O and S after OAS: O-N-AS-S-IS. Jacqueline Kennedy became Jackie Onassis.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis was the US First Lady before marrying Aristotle Onassis.

clue.text: What's deer on?

parts.note: a hind is a female deer and in cricket the on side is the leg side

explanation.surface: Asks what a deer is standing on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'deer on' becomes hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer stands on its rear limbs, and hind is also the female deer.

clue.text: Unusually impersonal since snuffing out flame …

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters are put in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A detached manner, oddly, since the fire was put out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the act itself: killing a lover, the flame, in a fit of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime of passion is typically killing a lover, a romantic flame, in jealous rage.

clue.text: … lit in campaign — it edified

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A light was kindled during an inspiring crusade.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across campaIGN IT EDified.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited means set alight or kindled, the same as lit.

clue.text: Egyptian king levels housing for yours truly

indicators.note: housing means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rases means levels to the ground, demolishes
yours truly means the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A pharaoh demolishes homes for the writer's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes inside RASES: RA-ME-SES. Rameses was the name of several pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses the Great was a powerful pharaoh of ancient Egypt, one of eleven of that name.
